questions.question: Traffic signals sometimes show arrows to control turns from certain lanes. What does a green arrow mean?

options.text: It is used only on one-way streets.
It means the same as a green light, but you must turn in the direction the arrow shows.
You may proceed only if the green arrow appears with a circular green light.
It shows the way to an airport.

questions.correctAnswerText: It means the same as a green light, but you must turn in the direction the arrow shows.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means the same as a circular green light. However, traffic in that lane must turn in the direction shown by the arrow.

questions.question: When must you yield for emergency vehicles?

options.text: Never.
When you see flashing red or blue lights or hear a siren.
Only when other vehicles yield first.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you see flashing red or blue lights or hear a siren.
questions.explanation: You must yield to any emergency vehicle using its siren or flashing lights.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: There is a detour ahead.
You must stop for flaggers.
The road ahead is closed.
Road work is happening ahead.

questions.explanation: Construction and maintenance signs are orange. They warn drivers about unusual or dangerous conditions in work areas. This sign tells you to slow down and drive carefully as you approach the construction zone.

questions.question: You are in an accident and someone is injured. What should you do?

options.text: Move the injured person away from the scene right away.
Always leave the injured person where they are.
Do not move the injured person unless necessary. Keep them warm and give first aid.
Stay away from the injured person.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not move the injured person unless necessary. Keep them warm and give first aid.
questions.explanation: Do not move injured people unless you must. Moving them without training can make injuries worse. Keep them warm until help arrives. If there is heavy bleeding, use direct pressure to stop it.

questions.question: All motor vehicles in Minnesota must have liability insurance.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: You must carry proof of insurance in your vehicle at all times. If you cannot show proof of insurance to a police officer, your driver license and vehicle registration may be suspended.

questions.question: When should you increase your following distance?

options.text: When driving behind a large vehicle that blocks your view.
When exiting an expressway.
When following a motorcycle.
In all of these situations.

questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when behind a large vehicle that blocks your view, in bad weather or heavy traffic, when exiting an expressway, when behind a motorcycle or bicycle, and when someone is tailgating you.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Do not enter.
No parking.
No U-turn.
No left turn.

questions.explanation: This sign means U-turns are not allowed at this location.

questions.question: How can you reduce the risk of hydroplaning?

options.text: Drive through shallow water.
Drive faster.
Drive slower.
Drive through deep water.

questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when you drive too fast in wet conditions. Driving slower reduces the risk of hydroplaning.

questions.question: Traffic moving in opposite directions is divided by what color lines?

options.text: White
Red
Black
Yellow

questions.explanation: Yellow lines divide traffic moving in opposite directions.

questions.question: What should you do if you stop at a railroad crossing with more than one track?

options.text: Wait until you can see all tracks clearly before driving.
Stop on the first track and watch for another train.
Go through as soon as the train passes.
Go through when one track is free.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until you can see all tracks clearly before driving.
questions.explanation: At a railroad crossing with more than one track, do not move as soon as a train passes. Wait until you can see all tracks clearly before crossing. Even with one track, check again for another approaching train before crossing.

questions.question: Can drivers pass on a two-lane road with a single solid yellow line on their side?

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: You can only pass when the broken yellow line is on your side. A solid yellow line on your side means you cannot pass.

questions.question: At night, another vehicle is coming toward you. What should your headlights be set to?

options.text: High beam
Low beam
Off, using only parking lights
Either high or low beam

questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights when another vehicle is approaching or ahead of you at night. High beams can blind other drivers and cause accidents.

questions.question: When must you stop for a school bus?

options.text: When it is parked on the road shoulder and empty
When it approaches you, even without flashing lights
On a two-lane highway when its red lights are flashing
Whenever the driver waves at you

questions.correctAnswerText: On a two-lane highway when its red lights are flashing
questions.explanation: You must stop when a school bus has flashing red lights and is picking up or dropping off children. On a two-lane road, all traffic in both directions must stop.

questions.question: Which light means you should slow down and be careful at an intersection?

options.text: A flashing yellow light
A flashing red light
A solid yellow light
A solid red light

questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down, look both ways, and be ready to stop.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: These parking spaces are for people with disabled parking permits
A roundabout is ahead
You must turn in the direction of the arrow
These lanes are for buses and carpool vehicles

questions.correctAnswerText: These parking spaces are for people with disabled parking permits
questions.explanation: This sign shows that parking spaces are reserved only for vehicles displaying a disabled parking permit.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You are entering a one-way street the wrong way
School crossing ahead
Do not drive in this lane
Left-turning traffic must yield to oncoming cars even on a green light

questions.correctAnswerText: Left-turning traffic must yield to oncoming cars even on a green light
questions.explanation: This sign means that drivers turning left do not have the right-of-way. You must wait for oncoming traffic to pass before turning.

questions.question: A regulatory sign with a red circle and slash through it means:

options.text: Come to a complete stop
This action is not allowed
Some drivers must yield to others
Drive slower than the speed limit

questions.explanation: A red circle with a slash is a prohibition sign. It means the action shown is forbidden.

questions.question: A flashing red traffic light works the same way as:

options.text: A slow sign
A yield sign
A stop sign
An intersection sign

questions.explanation: A flashing red light means you must stop completely and let all other traffic go first, just like a stop sign.

questions.question: Can you drink alcohol in a car on a public highway?

options.text: Yes, as long as you are not driving
Yes, if you are in the back seat
Yes, if you are in the back of a pickup truck
No, never

questions.explanation: It is illegal to drink alcohol or have an open bottle in a vehicle on any public road. This applies to all passengers and situations.

questions.question: What does a red arrow on a traffic light mean?

options.text: Proceed slowly through the intersection
Stop, then go when the road is clear
Stop, then go when the light turns green
You may turn in the direction the arrow points

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop, then go when the light turns green
questions.explanation: A red arrow means stop and stay stopped until a green light or green arrow appears.

questions.question: Drivers do not have to yield to pedestrians who are crossing against the traffic light.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: You must always yield to pedestrians. Some pedestrians may cross against the light by mistake.

questions.question: When dealing with pedestrians, a driver must:

options.text: Make sure the pedestrian sees your vehicle.
Always yield the right-of-way, even if the pedestrian is wrong.
Yield only when the pedestrian has the legal right to cross.
Slow down and honk your horn at crosswalks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always yield the right-of-way, even if the pedestrian is wrong.
questions.explanation: You must do everything possible to prevent hitting a pedestrian, no matter what. Always watch for pedestrians and give them the right-of-way, even if they are crossing in the wrong place.

questions.question: A driver entering interstate traffic from an entrance or acceleration ramp:

options.text: Should yield to drivers already on the interstate.
Has the right-of-way.
May force their way into traffic.
Can assume other drivers will make room.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should yield to drivers already on the interstate.
questions.explanation: When entering the interstate from a ramp, you must yield to traffic already on the highway. Merge safely when you have an opening.

questions.question: Driving at night requires extra caution because:

options.text: Traffic moves faster at night.
There is more traffic at night.
Drivers cannot see as well at night.
Accidents happen more often at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers cannot see as well at night.
questions.explanation: It is dark at night, so drivers cannot see as well. You must use your headlights from 30 minutes after sunset until 30 minutes before sunrise, or whenever people and vehicles are not visible for 500 feet.

questions.question: Two solid yellow lines on the road mean:

options.text: Passing is allowed from both directions.
Passing is not allowed.
Passing is allowed at the top of a hill.
Passing is allowed during the day only.

questions.explanation: Yellow lines mean traffic on the other side is moving toward you. Never cross two solid yellow lines to pass from either direction.

questions.question: A solid yellow line on your side of the centerline means:

options.text: Slow down.
Pass with caution.
Do not pass.
Keep right on hills.

questions.explanation: A solid yellow line next to your lane means you cannot pass.

questions.question: When turning left at an intersection, a driver must yield to a bicyclist coming from the opposite direction.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: When turning left at an intersection, yield to bikes coming toward you just as you would for cars. Keep your wheels straight while waiting and go when the road is clear.

questions.question: If an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaches while you are on a one-way street, you must:

options.text: Turn on your flashers.
Drive to the nearest side of the road and stop.
Speed up and take the nearest exit.
Slow down until it passes you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the nearest side of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaches on a one-way street, drive to the nearest roadside and stop.

questions.question: When passing other vehicles:

options.text: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
Honk your horn at least three times.
Return to your lane within 10 feet of the other vehicle.
You do not need to signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors and blind spots before passing. Use your turn signal before changing lanes. Return to your lane when you can see the front of the passed vehicle in your mirror.

questions.question: When driving on icy or snowy roads, which technique will help prevent crashes?

options.text: Add extra weight to your vehicle for better grip.
Get off the highway as fast as you can.
Use four-wheel drive.
Slow down and stay farther behind other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and stay farther behind other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Reduce your speed on snowy or icy roads. Slowing down and keeping a greater distance behind other vehicles are the best ways to avoid crashes in these conditions.
